verses.verse:
तिस्रोऽवस्थाश्च तेषां स्युः साध्या सिद्धा रसप्रदा।
आद्ये विस्तारतानेषु गीतेषु च रसप्रदा।१०६।
verses.text: They have three states: sādhyā (to be attained), siddhā (attained) and rasapradā (giving rasa). The first [two belong] to vistāra (elaboration) and tānas, and the rasapradā to songs.

commentary.text: If alaṅkāras (patterned exercises) are composed in three notes by the rule of mathematics, using only ekāvṛtti (one-note repetition) with the help of laṅghana (skipping), the following 36 alaṅkāras can be composed.
SaReGaGa SaSaReGa SaReReGa SaGaReGa SaReSaGa - from Sa to Ga --- 5+
SaGaReRe SaSaGaRe SaGaGaRe SaReGaRe SaGaSaRe - from Sa to Re --- 5+
SaReGaSa SaGaReSa  - from Sa to Sa -- 2 = 12
In the same way, beginning from Re and from Ga, there will be 12*3=36 in all.

following.text: When I have to build tānas (fast melodic runs) in a particular rāga, I have to maintain the qualities of the rāga and their jātis (classes by number of notes). In such a situation it is difficult to carry through alaṅkāras (patterned exercises). To get over this difficulty, [we] attend to the subtle elements within the alaṅkāras, and carry those same elements through in the tānas.
